title: Strategic dependency pin + SDK surface hygiene for Python/JS/Go clients
creator: Diego Marin
description:
Scope: Coordinate a cross-language (Python, JS, Go) dependency upgrade and API surface cleanup focused on removing legacy request parameters, tightening semver pins, and ensuring backwards-compatible client behavior for production customers.

Goals:
- Bump critical transitive dependencies (http client libs, JSON serializers, test harnesses) to versions that address known security/bug issues and provide better performance.
- Remove or flag legacy API params that are deprecated (old callback-style fields, legacy transport flags).
- Provide compatibility shims where necessary and publish migration guides and changelogs.
- Run performance and integration benchmarks to verify token latency and throughput remain within SLOs.
- Roll out via canary releases and automated incompatibility detection in CI.

Outcomes expected:
- Reduced SDK install surface and clearer migration path for users.
- Lowered runtime tail latency in Python and Go clients by adopting newer HTTP client behavior and connection pooling fixes.
- No high-severity regressions for existing hosted API customers.

Milestones / Tasks:
1) Create dependency matrix for all three clients (owners: Aisha/Diego). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/SDK+Dependency+Matrix
2) Prototype upgrade in forked Python client, run unit + integration tests against staging runtime. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/1891
3) Apply equivalent upgrades to JS (node-fetch -> undici) and Go (net/http patches) with compatibility flags. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/987, https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/412
4) Add feature flags and compatibility layer for deprecated params: expose WARN logs for 2 cycles before removal.
5) Run perf suite (load, tail-latency, long-context KV-cache) against dedicated staging: dashboard https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/sdk-client-upgrades
6) Publish migration guide and deprecation timeline to docs and changelog.
7) Canary release to 5% of traffic, monitor errors and latency for 72 hours, then ramp if green.

Rollout Risks:
- Edge-case consumers relying on deprecated field ordering or implicit coercions. Mitigation: run corpus of 50 top customers' integration tests and add automated smoke tests.
- Transitive dep behavior changes (timeouts, keepalives) affecting connection reuse. Mitigation: tune HTTP pool settings and add e2e load tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- All three language clients pass integration suite against runtime-1.20 staging with no >0.5% new error rate.
- Latency SLO (p50/p95) change <5% compared to baseline on Grafana dashboards.
- Migration guide and changelog published and linked from SDK docs.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Initial dependency matrix draft uploaded to Confluence. Noted two critical transitive upgrades: urllib3 in python and node-fetch replacement in JS.
2026-03-02 - Python PR opened (python-sdk#1891). Early unit failures due to stricter JSON decoding; added compatibility flag `allow_legacy_json` behind env var.
2026-03-04 - Design review w/ PM (Lena Zhou): agreed to 2-cycle deprecation window and WARN logs plus telemetry for any use of legacy params. Action: add telemetry event 'sdk.legacy_param_used'.

2026-03-07 - Load test run completed against staging (1000 rps for 30m). Observed 3% p95 increase in python p95; root cause: new HTTP client default socket timeout. Patch landed in python-sdk#1896 to tune pool settings.
2026-03-09 - Security review kickoff. Dependency audit flagged CVE-2025-2111 in old go-http-proxy; updated to v1.3.2 in go-sdk PR #412. Review asked for SBOM update for all three clients.
2026-03-11 - QA smoke: JS client undici migration passed integration; found one flaky test in CI related to streaming cancellation — added deterministic teardown in js-sdk#989.

2026-03-14 - Canary plan approved by SRE and Product. Target: start 2026-03-20 at 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% over 3 days if metrics green. Linked runbook and rollback PRs created: python rollback PR 1905, js rollback PR 1001, go rollback PR 419.
